AcmeCorp Support: Hey team, we're seeing a regression in streaming p95 TTFB starting ~08:20 UTC. Non-stream (sync) p95 is unchanged. Sample request id: rq_0abC123. ~10% of streams have first byte >1200ms, total time normal-ish (~2.2s). Endpoint: POST /v1/streams/generate (SSE). Any quick checks?

maya (support): thanks — can you paste the exact curl you used + the request id and a short log snippet? we can escalate once we have repro.

AcmeCorp Support: curl we used:
```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-..." -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":256}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams/generate
```
Log sample (from our edge): `edge-12 | rq=rq_0abC123 | ttfb=1320ms | total=2200ms | downstream=client`

ahmed (support): are you on HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 from the client? also are you using any CDN in front of us?

AcmeCorp Support: client is a browser using EventSource (so HTTP/1.1 via our proxy). We do have a lightweight CDN (FastEdge) in front that terminates TLS and forwards to your edge.

rachel (eng-runtime): thanks — this pattern smells like downstream/proxy coalescing/buffering of small chunks. If the edge or CDN buffers until a minimum chunk size or timeout, it inflates TTFB for streaming but not for non-stream (which sends a bigger first frame). Can you reproduce with a direct curl to api.redwood.com (bypass CDN)? also try `curl -N --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream"` and `curl -N --http2` to compare.

AcmeCorp Support: tried direct to api.redwood.com (no CDN) and still see occasional ttfb spikes but less frequent (3%). With `--http2` it's better. With `--http1.1` we see the 1.2s more.

rachel (eng-runtime): ok that confirms interplay of HTTP version + client path. We pushed a change in the edge runtime last week that adjusted chunk coalescing: it increased min_chunk_bytes from 256 -> 1024 to reduce networking overhead. That would explain more delayed first-chunk behavior for small outputs.

infra-bot: New trace created: trace/2149001111/rq_0abC123 (link: https://internal.redwood/trace/2149001111/rq_0abC123)

josh (eng-sre): can we get the streaming config for AcmeCorp route? if min_chunk_bytes is 1024 on their route, they hit the threshold. Immediate mitigations: 1) per-customer toggle to set min_chunk_bytes=256 or 0 (early flush), 2) temporary route to non-stream API for that customer, 3) suggest client switch to HTTP/2 where possible.

maya (support): AcmeCorp — we can flip a per-customer early-flush toggle in Console. Would you prefer we try min_chunk_bytes=0 (flush everything immediately) or 256? 0 will increase token write overhead but fixes latency.

AcmeCorp Support: please try min_chunk_bytes=0 for our tenant. We'll monitor for any regressions.

ahmed (support): done. I toggled `streaming.chunk_min_bytes=0` on AcmeCorp route at 08:52 UTC. Please verify.

AcmeCorp Support: confirming — first-byte p95 dropped from ~1200ms to ~180ms across the board in the next 10 minutes. Looks promising.

rachel (eng-runtime): good. Root cause = config rollout that increased coalescing threshold. For a durable fix we should: 1) revert or make the change opt-in, 2) add per-tenant defaults based on client protocol detection (e.g., browsers default to lower threshold), 3) add an automatic early-flush heuristic for small first-token outputs.

josh (eng-sre): i'm going to open an ops incident to track the edge config rollout and revert plan. Impact was limited to streaming TTFB on HTTP/1.1 client paths AND customers behind CDNs that buffer small chunks.

rachel (eng-runtime): engineering action items:
- Short term (<=4h): keep per-customer toggle and notify support playbook. Support to apply toggles for affected tenants.
- Mid term (<=48h): canary a runtime change that sets `min_chunk_bytes=256` globally but respects a console toggle.
- Long term: implement protocol-aware defaults and add a kep (kernel/socket) keepalive flush path to avoid relying on downstream buffering.

maya (support): noted. I'll add a KB entry: "Streaming TTFB spikes caused by edge chunk coalescing; mitigation: per-tenant chunk_min_bytes toggle or HTTP/2 client."

AcmeCorp Support: huge thanks — we'll leave the toggle on for now. Can you notify when the 48h change is scheduled so we can plan?

rachel (eng-runtime): will share schedule in this thread once patch is scheduled. Tentative canary tomorrow 08:00 UTC.

josh (eng-sre): also adding a quick test to CI that exercise small-first-chunk streaming under HTTP/1.1 to catch regressions.

AcmeCorp Support: closing loop — perf back to expected with toggle. Please keep us posted. :thumbsup:

maya (support): closing the escalation, marking follow-up tickets: ENG-3489 (runtime canary), SRE-872 (edge rollback audit), DOCS-191 (KB entry).
